text: Agent should present multiple options with pros/cons before acting on decisions with multiple viable paths, instead of picking one and forcing it through. Example: Google Search Console verification — agent picked HTML meta tag, modified code, committed, pushed — all without asking which method the user preferred.

Agent put feedback file in context/ folder (brand positioning) instead of workspace/ (working materials). Wrong folder — context/ is for brand identity and voice, workspace/ is for operational stuff like agent feedback.
Agent should use the business-meta-workflow skill (add_signal.py etc.) for capturing operational feedback, not create ad-hoc .md files. User had to correct this twice — wrong folder AND wrong format.
Site wasn't appearing in Google because base_url in site.yaml pointed to salemmalibary.com while the actual domain is salem.australia-gpa.com. robots.txt and sitemap.xml were also wrong.

Google Search Console verification method — HTML file upload was the easiest. The HTML meta tag approach didn't work (Jaspr Document meta parameter didn't render the tag in output). HTML file in web/ just works as static.

Workflows created by business-meta-workflow skill don't auto-invoke. The skill captures signals and detects patterns, but once a workflow is created, it just sits as a file. Nothing triggers it when a matching situation arises. The skill needs a mechanism to load relevant workflows at session start or when situations match — otherwise the whole cycle breaks at the 'Implement + Review' step.

Workflows have no usage tracking — no use_count field, no script to increment it, no way to know when a workflow hits the 5-use graduation threshold. The skill references '5+ runs without changes' for automation readiness but has no mechanism to count runs.

Architecture decision: Workflow graduation pipeline. Stages: Signal → Pattern → Workflow (young, manual) → Workflow (proven, 5+ uses) → Graduates to own Skill (auto-triggers). Meta-workflow skill owns capture+creation. Graduated skills own enforcement. Need: use_count tracking, graduate_workflow.py script, skill scaffolding. Decision made by Salem after discussion — not forced by agent.

Project organization feels too complex — hard to find things manually, relies entirely on AI to navigate. Uncertainty about when to split something into its own folder vs keep it with related stuff. No clear rule or mental model for folder decisions.

Conflict between context/ and workspace/ — both feel like they should be a central reference point but they serve different purposes. Wants a single central place for operational knowledge but current structure splits it. Tension between brand context (context/) and operational working materials (workspace/).

Specific example: build.sh, preview.md, wrangler.toml are website-specific but live at project root. If the project grows beyond the website, root becomes cluttered with website artifacts. Wants a rule/principle for when things should be moved closer to their scope.

Anything weird today? → Jaspr Document meta parameter didn't render google-site-verification tag — had to use HTML file method instead. Also found two skill directories (.agents/ and .pi/) that should have been one.
Anything repeating? → Agent making decisions without presenting options came up multiple times. Project structure/folder organization is a recurring pain.
Anything you want to change? → Agent should present options before acting. Agent should use business-meta-workflow skill scripts for capturing feedback, not ad-hoc files.

decisions.jsonl is never written to — no script logs architectural/strategic decisions. Only graduate_workflow.py writes there, which hasn't been used yet. All the decisions made today (graduation pipeline, folder moves) were not persisted as decisions.

patterns.jsonl is never written to — auto_scan.py detects patterns in-memory but never persists them. The file stays empty. Once a pattern is acted on (e.g. creating a workflow from a pattern), it should be logged so auto_scan can skip it next time.

Workflow and its data store should be connected. The decision workflow and decisions.jsonl were created separately but never linked — the workflow should include a step that writes to the data store. Same principle applies: any workflow that produces a recordable outcome should have a step that persists it.
